records.speaker: King
records.localization_note: King matches the ruler Rafael addresses as Your Majesty. Their audience establishes his authority over Portugal.
records.context: The king thanks Rafael, offers to reward him, and hears him defer the reward while Portugal is rebuilding. The king explains what the Proofs could mean for the Portuguese Crown, and tells Rafael to keep them out of Spain’s hands.

records.speaker: Local Lord
records.localization_note: Local Lord preserves the territorial scope of the original title and distinguishes this palace role from a king.
records.context: The original palace dispatch supplies the regional actor. The clean role label provides the title.

records.speaker: King
records.localization_note: King matches the clean palace role and the verified Istanbul audience. The English does not assign a personal identity to this general role.
records.context: The original palace dispatch supplies the regional actor. The clean role label provides the title.

records.speaker: Local King
records.localization_note: Local King preserves the distinction between the regional ruler and the other native royal title. It keeps the rank of king.
records.context: The original palace dispatch supplies the regional actor. The clean role label provides the title.

records.speaker: Magistrate
records.source_meaning: The official in charge of a county.
records.localization_note: Magistrate fits the office being impersonated when orders are given to arrest the smugglers. The reveal stays in the dialogue.
records.context: People posing as missionaries are exposed by a party led by an apparent magistrate. The governor and crew react differently to the staged intervention.

records.speaker: Daimyo
records.source_meaning: A daimyo, a Japanese territorial lord.
records.localization_note: Daimyo keeps the original title. The glass and castle scenes show his authority without making him the sovereign of Japan.
records.context: The daimyo learns what giyaman is and tells the guildmaster to collect it.

records.speaker: Governor
records.localization_note: Governor matches both the Escante discussion and Macao’s own political setting. The surrounding dialogue supplies the relevant jurisdiction.
records.context: The governor describes Escante’s failed coup and relays a rumor about the treasure key. People posing as missionaries are exposed by a party led by an apparent magistrate. The governor and crew react differently to the staged intervention.

records.speaker: Officiant
records.source_meaning: The person presiding over the rite.
records.localization_note: Officiant fits the person who performs rites and formally presents the Proof clue. It allows the character to describe his own history of resistance without implying a particular clergy office.
records.context: A guard admits the fleet. A ritual speaker confers an object, and the crew reflects on who held it. A guildmaster, a shipwright and the ritual figure dispute each other’s taste in paintings. The shopkeeper describes the new fashion. A speaker who confers the Proof clue describes resistance to Ottoman rule and points Hodram to ruins in Turkey. A guard recognizes Maria’s fleet and a ritual speaker formally confers the object.

records.speaker: Shaman
records.source_meaning: A ritual practitioner who leads invocations.
records.localization_note: Shaman describes the regional ritual practitioner selected for the original ceremony, whose function includes leading ritual acts.
records.context: The original ritual dispatch supplies the regional actor. The clean role label provides the title.

records.speaker: Senior Monk
records.localization_note: Senior Monk conveys the standing in the Japanese title. It leaves the office of the selected religious figure unspecified.
records.context: The original ritual dispatch supplies the regional actor. The clean role label provides the title.

records.speaker: Officiant
records.source_meaning: A person who presides over ritual observances.
records.localization_note: Officiant keeps the original role in both the temple encounter and the Guam story. The temple guardian explains a sacred tradition, and the man asking for passage has no stated clergy affiliation.
records.context: The temple guardian demands knowledge of the Vedas, hears the party’s explanation, and entrusts them with a coin after recognizing their text. The temple guardian recognizes the Veda Rafael brings back and offers a coin. Rafael must work out what it means. A port worker asks Maria to take a shipwrecked man home. The man thanks her in the words the worker taught him. Maria brings the man home to Guam. He thanks her and gives her a parting gift.

records.speaker: Senior Monk
records.localization_note: Senior Monk suits the monk who corrects Lil’s manners and requests supplies as offerings. His exact institutional office is unspecified.
records.context: A senior monk corrects Lil’s manners and asks her to bring tea and sugar for the offerings.

records.speaker: Senior Monk
records.localization_note: Senior Monk fits the elder who tests the captains’ intentions and helps them understand the Proof, without inventing an abbot’s office.
records.context: A senior monk tests Rafael’s intentions and tells him where the clan carrying the map went, with a warning about the danger and the Proof. The senior monk recounts the Yuan invasion and asks Hodram to bring back the emperor’s keepsake.

records.speaker: Shaman
records.source_meaning: A ritual practitioner who leads invocations.
records.localization_note: Shaman names the ceremonial function of this original regional variant and leaves the rite to explain the character’s actions.
records.context: The original ritual dispatch supplies the regional actor. The clean role label provides the title.

records.speaker: Priest
records.localization_note: Priest fits the title 神父. The mission sequence names the Society of Jesus, and the dialogue reveals who is posing as its representatives.
records.context: The priest acknowledges Rafael’s standing in the Mediterranean and presents the cloth. The crew reasons about what it might show. People posing as missionaries are exposed by a party led by an apparent magistrate. The governor and crew react differently to the staged intervention.

SC0 B79.summary: The priest acknowledges Rafael’s standing in the Mediterranean and presents the cloth. The crew reasons about what it might show.

speeches.Japanese:
FA殿
やりましたな。よくぞ、この地中海で
覇者となられましたな
それでは、お受けくだされ
speeches.English:
Mr. FA, you've done it!
 You've truly won supremacy 
 in the Mediterranean. Please,
 accept this.

speeches.Japanese:
ふう
…長かったな
speeches.English: Whew... At last.

speeches.Japanese:
これもきっと『覇者の証』の地図ですね
地中海の宝は、確か、何かの
『冠』のはずです…
speeches.English:
This must be another map to a Proof
 of Conquest. If I remember 
 correctly, the Mediterranean 
 treasure is some kind of crown...

speeches.Japanese:
よし、そいつを探せばいいんだな
行くぜ！
speeches.English:
All right, that's what we've got 
 to find. Let's go!

speeches.Japanese:
…？
でも、この布に書いてある模様
全然地図のようには見えないん
だけど…
speeches.English:
But this pattern on the cloth looks
 nothing like a map...

SC0 B116.summary: The temple guardian demands knowledge of the Vedas, hears the party’s explanation, and entrusts them with a coin after recognizing their text.

speeches.Japanese: ん！？　誰かいるぞ！
speeches.English: Hm? Someone's there!

speeches.Japanese:
まさか、人に会うことに
なろうとはのう…
speeches.English:
I never thought I would meet 
 anyone here...

speeches.Japanese: あの…、あなたは？
speeches.English: Um... who are you?

speeches.Japanese:
見ての通り
この遺跡を守っておる
speeches.English: As you can see, I guard these ruins.

speeches.Japanese: この遺跡はいったい…？
speeches.English: What is this place?

speeches.Japanese:
もともとスールヤバルマン２世が
ヴィシュヌと融合して
神になるために建造した
寺院なのじゃ
speeches.English:
It was originally built as a temple
 for Suryavarman II to unite
 with Vishnu and become a god.

speeches.Japanese:
スール…？　ヴィシュ…？
あー、なんだか全然分かんねえ！
speeches.English:
Surya...? Vish...? Bah, none 
 of that makes sense!

speeches.Japanese:
『ヴェーダ』を知らぬ者を近づける
わけにはいかぬ
…立ち去るのじゃ
speeches.English:
Those who know not the Vedas 
 may not approach. Leave.

speeches.Japanese:
どうすれば、あの人に認めて
もらえるんだろう？
『ヴェーダ』…っていったい…？
speeches.English:
How can we earn his approval?
 And what are the Vedas?

speeches.Japanese:
インド近辺で信仰されている
ヒンドゥー教のもとになった
神話ではないかと思いますが…
speeches.English:
I believe they're the myths
 that form the basis of Hinduism, 
 the religion practiced in India
 and the surrounding regions...

speeches.Japanese:
ヴィシュヌはヒンドゥー教の
神の名ですね？
speeches.English: Vishnu is a Hindu god, correct?

speeches.Japanese: おお、よく知っておるな
speeches.English: Ah, you are well informed.
...Hm? What is that?!

speeches.Japanese:
ヴェーダの最初の原典ではないか！
そ、そなたらはいったい！？
speeches.English:
The very first text of the Vedas!
 W-who are you people?!

speeches.Japanese:
そうか…！　なるほど
ようやく現れたというわけか
こんな年端もいかぬ少年がのう…
speeches.English:
Ah... Now I see! So you've finally 
 come. Such a young boy, too...
Hm?

speeches.Japanese:
うむ
では、これをそなたたちに託すとしよう
speeches.English:
Very well. I shall entrust 
 this to you.

speeches.Japanese:
古いコイン…？
何ですか、これは？
speeches.English: An old coin? What is it?

speeches.Japanese:
わしの用は済んだ。あとは自分たちの
力で解き明かすのじゃ
さあ、行くがよいぞ
speeches.English:
My duty is done. Unravel the rest
 yourselves. Now go.

speeches.Japanese: どういうことだろう…？
speeches.English: What did he mean?

SC0 B120.summary: A senior monk tests Rafael’s intentions and tells him where the clan carrying the map went, with a warning about the danger and the Proof.

speeches.Japanese: もし
speeches.English: Excuse me.

speeches.Japanese:
え？
…何か？
speeches.English: Hm? Yes?

speeches.Japanese:
そなた、『覇者の証』なる宝物を
探し求めておるな？
speeches.English: You seek the Proof of Conquest?

speeches.Japanese:
！！
どうしてそれを？
speeches.English: How did you know?

speeches.Japanese:
あなたは、『証』の地図について
何かご存じの様子じゃのう
speeches.English:
You seem to know something 
 of the Proof's map.

speeches.Japanese:
いかにも…。しかし
誰にでもお教えできるものでは
ござりませぬぞ
speeches.English:
True. But this cannot be told
 to just anyone.

speeches.Japanese:
邪悪なる心を持つ者が
それを手にしたときのことを
恐れておられるのじゃな？
speeches.English:
You fear what an evil heart
 might do with it.

speeches.Japanese: …左様
speeches.English: Yes.

speeches.Japanese:
心配はご無用じゃ
私は長年の間
『証』について研究してまいった
speeches.English:
You need not worry. I have spent 
 many years studying the Proof.

speeches.Japanese:
この少年こそ、間違いなく
覇者の資格を持つ者と
確信しておりますぞ
speeches.English:
This boy surely has the makings
 of a conqueror.

speeches.Japanese: ふうむ…
speeches.English: Hmm...

speeches.Japanese:
お願いします
ご存じでしたら、どうか教えてください
speeches.English: Please. Tell us what you know.

speeches.Japanese: …よかろう
speeches.English: Very well.

speeches.Japanese:
その昔、中華の地において
地図を守ってきた一族は、時の権力者の
追跡を逃れ、はるか、はるか北東の地に
向かったという
speeches.English:
Long ago, a clan that guarded
 the map in China fled
 those in power and journeyed 
 far, far to the northeast, 
 so the story goes.

speeches.Japanese: はるか北東…ですか
speeches.English: Far to the northeast...?

speeches.Japanese:
北の果て、氷の海近くの小さき村に
たどり着いた一族の子孫は
そこで今もひっそりと暮らして
おるはずじゃ
speeches.English:
The clan reached a little village
 in the far north, near an icy sea. 
 Their descendants should still 
 be living quietly there.

speeches.Japanese: …中国のずっと北東の村、か
speeches.English: ...A village far northeast of China.

speeches.Japanese:
巨大な半島の付け根
東岸の高き峰のふもとを探すがよい
speeches.English:
Look at the base of an enormous
 peninsula, at the foot of a high 
 peak on its eastern coast.

speeches.Japanese:
あまりにも遠き地ゆえ、普通の船では
たどり着くことは難しいかもしれぬ
生半可な気持ちでは、そなたらの命は
ないぞ
speeches.English:
It may be too far for an ordinary
 ship to reach. If you take 
 this journey lightly, it will cost 
 you your lives.

speeches.Japanese: （…ごくっ。）
speeches.English: (...Gulp.)

speeches.Japanese:
よいか。決して邪心を持つ者に
『証』を渡してはならぬ
そなたも邪悪な欲望に囚われるで
ないぞ
speeches.English:
Listen well. Never give the Proof
 to anyone with evil intentions.
 And do not let evil desires take 
 hold of you, either.

speeches.Japanese:
はい！
ありがとうございました
speeches.English: Yes! Thank you.

SC0 B162.summary: A guard admits the fleet. A ritual speaker confers an object, and the crew reflects on who held it.

speeches.Japanese:
FOの者であるな
通るがよい
speeches.English:
You're with FO, I see. 
 You may pass.

speeches.Japanese:
地中海を統べるべき者よ
汝にこれを授く
speeches.English:
You shall rule the Mediterranean.
 I bestow this upon you.

speeches.Japanese: こいつはすげえ！！
speeches.English: Amazing!

speeches.Japanese: パシャ軍が持っていたのかな…
speeches.English:
I wonder if Pasha's forces 
 had this...

speeches.Japanese:
ハイレディン提督は
これを…
speeches.English: Admiral Hayreddin... This...

SC0 B164.summary: The king thanks Rafael, offers to reward him, and hears him defer the reward while Portugal is rebuilding.

speeches.Japanese:
FA様
国王陛下が、お待ちでございます
speeches.English: FA. His Majesty awaits.

speeches.Japanese:
おお、FAよ！
よくぞ、あのスペイン艦隊をうち破って
くれた！　予はこれより我が国の復興に
全力を尽くそうぞ！
speeches.English:
Ah, FA! Well done defeating
 that Spanish fleet. I'll devote all
 my strength to rebuilding Portugal.

speeches.Japanese:
はっ。私の念願がひとつ叶いました
これからもポルトガルの名に恥じぬよう
努力いたします
speeches.English:
Yes, Your Majesty. 
 One of my dearest wishes 
 has come true. I will keep doing 
 all I can to honor Portugal.

speeches.Japanese:
うむ。よくぞ言ってくれた
そなたは、祖国の恩人じゃ！
speeches.English:
Well said. Your country owes 
 you a great debt.

speeches.Japanese:
お褒めにあずかり光栄に存じます
ですが…
speeches.English: I'm honored, Your Majesty. But...

speeches.Japanese:
おお！　そうじゃったそうじゃった
そなたらは世界をまたにかけて
エシュタードを拡げる旅を続けて
おるんじゃったな
speeches.English:
Ah, of course! You've been sailing 
 the world to expand the Estado.

speeches.Japanese:
仰せの通りにございます
未だ、決着がついていない仕事も
残っておりますゆえ…
speeches.English:
As you say, Your Majesty. We still 
 have work to finish...

speeches.Japanese:
うむ。思う存分精進するがよいぞ
そうじゃな、何か褒美を取らせよう
speeches.English:
Very well. Give it your best. Now, 
 I should like to reward you.

speeches.Japanese:
『証』の件であろう
そなたには何かと労をかけておる
じゃが、頼れるのはそなたしか
おらぬのじゃ
speeches.English:
The Proofs, you mean.
 I've asked a great deal of you.
 You're the only one I can turn to.

speeches.Japanese:
必ずや
なしとげてご覧に入れましょう
speeches.English: I will see it through, Your Majesty.

speeches.Japanese:
うむ。楽しみに待っておるぞ
そうじゃな、何か褒美を取らせよう
speeches.English:
I look forward to it. Now, 
 I should like to reward you.

speeches.Japanese:
いえ、今は王国の再建に何かと物いりで
ございましょう
私のことはお気遣いなさいませぬよう…
speeches.English:
Rebuilding the kingdom will take 
 a great deal, Your Majesty.
 Please don't concern yourself
 with a reward for me.

speeches.Japanese:
（バカヤロウ！
　もらえるもんは、もらっとけ！）
speeches.English: (You idiot! Take the reward!)

speeches.Japanese:
ううむ。どこまでも遠慮深いことじゃ…
確かに国がこのような状態では
そなたの功の大きさに充分報いることが
できぬ
speeches.English:
Always so modest... In our present 
 state, we truly can't give 
 you a reward equal to what 
 you've done.

speeches.Japanese:
そうじゃな
そなたが真の目的を達成して帰って
くるまでに考えておくこととしよう
speeches.English:
Very well. I'll think it over
 while you see your task through
 and make your way home.

speeches.Japanese: ありがたきお言葉
speeches.English: You are most kind, Your Majesty.

speeches.Japanese:
うむ
あまり引き留めるのもなんじゃな
では、さらばじゃ
speeches.English:
I suppose I shouldn't keep 
 you any longer. Farewell.

speeches.Japanese: はっ。それでは失礼いたします
speeches.English: Yes, Your Majesty. By your leave.

speeches.Japanese:
かぁーっ！　惜しいことしやがるな～
ったく、FIはよー
欲がねえなあ
speeches.English:
What a waste! Honestly, FI,
 you don't want anything
 for yourself, do you?

speeches.Japanese:
今はご褒美よりも大切な仕事が
残っているからね
speeches.English:
We've got something more important 
 to do right now than collect 
 a reward.

speeches.Japanese:
それもそうか…
さあ、エシュタード制覇の仕上げだ！
行くぜ！　FI提督！！
speeches.English:
Fair enough... Let's finish taking 
 control of the Estado! Onward, 
 Admiral FI!

SC0 B165.summary: The king explains what the Proofs could mean for the Portuguese Crown, and tells Rafael to keep them out of Spain’s hands.

speeches.Japanese:
FIよ
よくぞ来た
speeches.English:
Welcome, FI. 
 I'm glad you've come.

speeches.Japanese: お召しにございますか？
speeches.English: You sent for me, Your Majesty?

speeches.Japanese:
他でもない
そちの探しておる宝の話じゃ
speeches.English: It's about the treasure you seek.

speeches.Japanese:
世界各地に７つ存在すると言われる
『覇者の証』。これを教皇に示せば
再びポルトガル王権の発効を
認めるよう交渉ができる
speeches.English:
The seven Proofs of Conquest 
 are said to be scattered 
 across the world.
 If we show them to the Pope, 
 we can ask him 
 to recognize the authority 
 of the Portuguese Crown again.

speeches.Japanese:
何よりも、国民すべてが再び団結
するために、海運立国ポルトガル再建の
象徴としてどうしても必要な
至宝なのじゃ
speeches.English:
Above all, we need that treasure 
 as a symbol of Portugal's rebirth
 as a seafaring nation. It can bring
 all our people together again.

speeches.Japanese:
ヨーロッパはもとより、世界の完全
制覇を目論むスペインには
間違っても渡してはならぬぞ
speeches.English:
Spain means to rule more than
 Europe. It wants the whole world.
 Whatever happens, keep the Proofs
 out of Spanish hands.

speeches.Japanese: よいな！
speeches.English: Is that clear?

speeches.Japanese: はい！
speeches.English: Yes!

SC0 B195.summary: A guildmaster, a shipwright and the ritual figure dispute each other’s taste in paintings. The shopkeeper describes the new fashion.

speeches.Japanese: ん？
speeches.English: Hm?

speeches.Japanese: 本当に素晴らしいよ！
speeches.English: Truly wonderful!

speeches.Japanese: そうかね？
speeches.English: You think so?

speeches.Japanese:
ああ、彼は後世に名を残す
芸術家になるね
speeches.English:
I do. He's an artist people
 will remember for generations.

speeches.Japanese: はあ
speeches.English: Ah.

speeches.Japanese:
君も今のうちに彼の作品を
手に入れておくといい
speeches.English:
You should buy his work
 while you can.

speeches.Japanese: 俺は、こっちの方がいいと思うがね！
speeches.English: Well, I think this one's better!

speeches.Japanese:
それも悪くはないが
彼の作品にはかなわないよ
speeches.English: Not bad, but no match for his work.

speeches.Japanese:
何を言っているんだ、君たち
それより、あっちの方が
いい作品に決まっておる
speeches.English:
What are you two talking about?
 That one over there is clearly 
 the finest.

speeches.Japanese:
何と言われても
私は彼の絵を購入する！
speeches.English:
Say what you like. I'm buying
 his painting!

speeches.Japanese:
俺はこの絵を描いた画家のものを
もらうぞ！
speeches.English: I'll take one by this artist!

speeches.Japanese: 私はこちらをもらおう！
speeches.English: And I'll take this one!

speeches.Japanese: 毎度ありがとうございました
speeches.English: Thank you for your business.

speeches.Japanese: バタンッ！
speeches.English: Slam!

speeches.Japanese:
やっと帰ったか
毎度毎度、店の中で言い争うのは
やめてもらいたいな
speeches.English:
Finally, they're gone. I wish
 they'd quit arguing in here
 every time they come in.

speeches.Japanese: 店主、さっきのは何の騒ぎだ
speeches.English: What was that commotion?

speeches.Japanese: あれは、金持ちの道楽さ
speeches.English: Rich folks and their hobbies.

speeches.Japanese: 金持ちの道楽？
speeches.English: Their hobbies?

speeches.Japanese:
ああ、最近絵画を集めるのが
流行ってるのさ
speeches.English:
Yeah. Collecting paintings 
 is all the rage lately.

speeches.Japanese: へえ。高尚な趣味だな
speeches.English: A refined hobby.

speeches.Japanese:
まっ、本当に見る目のあるヤツは
少ないけどな
speeches.English:
Well, hardly any of them 
 have an eye for it.

speeches.Japanese: はっはっはははは、店主も言うね
speeches.English:
Ha ha! 
 You don't mince words, do you?

speeches.Japanese: おおっと、秘密にしといてくださいよ
speeches.English: Oops. Keep it between us, okay?

speeches.Japanese: 分かってるよ
speeches.English: Of course.

speeches.Japanese: バスラで絵画が流行しそうです
speeches.English: Artwork may catch on in Basra.

SC0 B200.summary: The daimyo learns what giyaman is and tells the guildmaster to collect it.

speeches.Japanese: 素晴らしい！　まさに芸術じゃ
speeches.English: Splendid! A work of art, truly.

speeches.Japanese: 仰せの通りにござる
speeches.English: As you say.

speeches.Japanese:
これほど素晴らしい品であるからには
さぞ名の通った職人が作ったので
あろうな
speeches.English:
A piece this fine must be
 the work of a master craftsman.

speeches.Japanese: さようでございます
speeches.English: Indeed.

speeches.Japanese:
うーむ
このような物が流行しておったとは
全く知らなんだ
speeches.English:
Hmm. I had no idea such things 
 had come into fashion.

speeches.Japanese: これは、何というものじゃ？
speeches.English: What is it called?

speeches.Japanese: ギヤマン（ガラス）にござりまする
speeches.English: It's called giyaman. Glass.

speeches.Japanese: ふーむ。ギヤマンとな
speeches.English: Hmm. Giyaman, you say.

speeches.Japanese:
よしっ、わしの収集に加える
街中のギヤマンを集めてまいれ
speeches.English:
Very well! 
 I'll add it to my collection.
 Go and bring me all
 the giyaman in town.

speeches.Japanese: ははっ、御意のままに
speeches.English: At once. As you command.

speeches.Japanese: 大坂でガラスが流行しそうです
speeches.English: Glass may catch on in Osaka.

SC0 B304.summary: The temple guardian recognizes the Veda Rafael brings back and offers a coin. Rafael must work out what it means.

speeches.Japanese: ん？　また来たのか？
speeches.English: Hm? Back again?

speeches.Japanese:
あなたが言っていた『ヴェーダ』と
いうのはこれのことですね？
speeches.English:
Is this what you meant when
 you told us about the Vedas?
...Hm? Is that what I think it is?!

speeches.Japanese:
まさしく
ヴェーダの最初の原典じゃ！
speeches.English:
It is! The original text 
 of the first Veda!

speeches.Japanese:
こんな年端もいかぬ少年が
これを持って現れるとは…
speeches.English:
To think someone as young
 as you would turn up with it...

speeches.Japanese:
では、これを
そなたたちに託すとしよう
speeches.English:
Well, then. I think I can entrust
 this to you.

speeches.Japanese:
古いコイン…？
何ですか、これは？
speeches.English: An old coin...? What is this?

speeches.Japanese:
わしの用は済んだ。あとは自分たちの
力で解き明かすのじゃ
さあ、行くがよいぞ
speeches.English:
My part is done. You'll
 have to puzzle out the rest
 yourselves. Go on, now.

speeches.Japanese: どういうことだろう…？
speeches.English: What did he mean by that...?

SC1 B120.summary: The senior monk recounts the Yuan invasion and asks Hodram to bring back the emperor’s keepsake.

speeches.Japanese: もし
speeches.English: Excuse me.

speeches.Japanese: …何か？
speeches.English: Yes?

speeches.Japanese:
そなた、『覇者の証』なる宝物を
探し求めておるな？
speeches.English:
You are searching for a treasure 
 known as the Proof of Conquest,
 are you not?

speeches.Japanese:
…
なぜそれを？
speeches.English: How do you know that?

speeches.Japanese:
そうか
見たところ、将兵をつかさどる
身分のようであるが？
speeches.English:
I see. And by the look 
 of you, you command soldiers?

speeches.Japanese:
確かに
国軍艦隊の統率を任されている…
それが何か？
speeches.English:
That's right. I've been entrusted
 with command of our national fleet.
 Why do you ask?

speeches.Japanese:
なるほどのう
では、話さねばなるまい…
speeches.English:
I see... Then I must tell
 you something.

speeches.Japanese:
この国は、その昔、史上最大の帝国と
された“元”の来襲を受けたことが
ある
speeches.English:
Long ago, this country was invaded 
 by the Yuan, said to be the largest
 empire in history.

speeches.Japanese:
大陸では無敵を誇った元軍であったが
神風の御加護により
日本はかろうじて
難を逃れることができた
speeches.English:
The Yuan army was invincible 
 on the mainland, 
 but with the protection
 of the divine winds, 
 Japan barely escaped disaster.

speeches.Japanese:
元帝が陸上軍だけではなく
海軍においても無敵であれば
世界制覇を成し得たかもしれぬ
speeches.English:
With an invincible navy too, 
 the Yuan emperor 
 might have conquered the world.

speeches.Japanese:
元帝のように偉業を成し遂げた
王たちの飽くなき壮図が
この『証』には
込められているとされておる
speeches.English:
The Proof is said to embody
 the boundless ambitions of kings 
 who accomplished great deeds, like 
 the Yuan emperor.

speeches.Japanese:
そなたが
元帝の遺志を継ぐ者であれば
その形見を手にするはずじゃ
speeches.English:
If you are to carry on the Yuan
 emperor's will, you should come
 into possession of his keepsake.

speeches.Japanese: 元帝の形見…
speeches.English: The Yuan emperor's keepsake...

speeches.Japanese:
それを持って、もう一度ここに
来られるがよかろう
speeches.English: Once you have it, come back here.

SC1 B153.summary: A speaker who confers the Proof clue describes resistance to Ottoman rule and points Hodram to ruins in Turkey.

speeches.Japanese:
FOの者だな
よし、通れ
speeches.English:
You're with FO. All 
 right, go through.

speeches.Japanese:
地中海を統べる者よ
汝にこれを授く
speeches.English:
You who rule the Mediterranean,
 I bestow this upon you.

speeches.Japanese: あなたは…？
speeches.English: You are...?

speeches.Japanese:
長い間、オスマンの支配に
抵抗してきた者じゃよ
speeches.English:
Someone who has long resisted
 Ottoman rule.

speeches.Japanese: では、あなたがセラたちを助けて？
speeches.English:
Then... were you the one who helped
 Sera and the others?

speeches.Japanese:
細かいことは聞かずともよかろう
さあ、それを解いて
早く『証』を探すのじゃ
speeches.English:
There's no need to concern yourself
 with the details. Now, 
 decipher it and find the Proof 
 without delay.

speeches.Japanese:
我らのようにオスマンの支配を
逃れた者たちは他にもおる
トルコにある遺跡を探しなされ
speeches.English:
There are others who escaped 
 Ottoman rule, as we did. Look
 for the ruins in Turkey.

SC2 B309.summary: A senior monk corrects Lil’s manners and asks her to bring tea and sugar for the offerings.

speeches.Japanese:
買ってきたわよー
あー、疲れた
speeches.English: I got it! Whew, I'm worn out.

speeches.Japanese: これ、休んでおる暇はないぞ
speeches.English: Now, now. There's no time to rest.

speeches.Japanese:
えーっ？
今度はなあにい？
speeches.English: Huh?! What is it now?

speeches.Japanese: 口のきき方がなっておらーん！
speeches.English: Mind your manners!

speeches.Japanese: …今度は何でしょう！
speeches.English:
...What would you like me
 to do next?

speeches.Japanese:
ふむ
茶と砂糖を用意するのじゃ
speeches.English: Hmm. Bring me some tea and sugar.

speeches.Japanese:
それもお供え物なの？
もしかして、これも自腹？
speeches.English:
Are those offerings too? Don't 
 tell me I've got to pay
 for these myself as well.

speeches.Japanese: 左様
speeches.English: Indeed.

speeches.Japanese:
なんで、仏教徒でもないあたしが
こんなことしなきゃならないの？
speeches.English:
Why do I have to do all this?
 I'm not even Buddhist!

speeches.Japanese: 文句は無用！
speeches.English: Enough complaining!

speeches.Japanese:
はいはい、お茶とお砂糖ね
買ってくればいいんでしょ！
speeches.English:
All right, all right.
 Tea and sugar. I'll go buy them!

SC3 B111.summary: A port worker asks Maria to take a shipwrecked man home. The man thanks her in the words the worker taught him.

speeches.Japanese:
姐さん、待ってやした
この人を、グアムっていう村まで
運んでいってくれやせんか？
speeches.English:
I've been waiting for you! 
 Could you take this fellow 
 to a village called Guam?

speeches.Japanese: どうしたの、この人？
speeches.English: What happened?

speeches.Japanese:
言葉が通じないんで、よく分からねえん
だが、丸木船で香料諸島に流れ着いた
らしいんで
speeches.English:
We don't speak the same language,
 so I'm not too sure. Seems 
 he drifted to the Spice Islands
 in a dugout canoe.

speeches.Japanese:
西洋人の船に忍び込んで、なんとか
ここまでたどり着いたものの、結局
帰れなくなっちまったらしいんでやす
speeches.English:
Then he stowed away on a Western 
 ship and somehow made it here. Now 
 he can't get home.

speeches.Japanese:
グアム…だったわね？
その村、どこにあるのかしら？
speeches.English: Guam, was it? Where is that village?

speeches.Japanese:
いやあ、俺に聞かれてもなあ。この人も
東北東の方角を指さすだけだし
speeches.English:
Beats me. He just keeps
 pointing east-northeast.

speeches.Japanese: …どうしようかしら
speeches.English: ...What should I do?

speeches.Japanese:
こんなこと、他に頼める人がいないんで
姐さん、お願いしますよ
speeches.English:
There's no one else I can ask. 
 Please, could you help him?

speeches.Japanese:
…時間がかかるかもしれないわ
それでもよければ、私の船に乗って
もらいましょう
speeches.English:
...It may take some time.
 If he doesn't mind 
 that, he can come aboard my ship.

speeches.Japanese: ありがてえ
speeches.English: Thank you!

speeches.Japanese: …シェシェ（謝謝）
speeches.English: ...Xie xie. (Thank you.)

speeches.Japanese: あら、中国語？
speeches.English: Chinese?

speeches.Japanese:
いやあ、俺が教えておいたんですよ
姐さんなら、絶対に引き受けてくれると
思いましてね
speeches.English:
Well, I taught him that. I figured 
 you'd take him, for sure.

speeches.Japanese: ずいぶん見込まれたものね
speeches.English:
You certainly have a lot 
 of faith in me.

speeches.Japanese: シェシェ
speeches.English: Xie xie.

SC3 B118.summary: A guard recognizes Maria’s fleet and a ritual speaker formally confers the object.

speeches.Japanese:
FOの者だな
よし、通れ
speeches.English:
You're with FO? All right,
 you may pass.

speeches.Japanese:
地中海を統べる者よ
汝にこれを授く
speeches.English:
Ruler of the Mediterranean,
 I bestow this upon you.

SC3 B125.summary: The governor describes Escante’s failed coup and relays a rumor about the treasure key.

speeches.Japanese:
おお
FA提督か
speeches.English: Oh, Admiral FA!

speeches.Japanese:
なんと、エスカンテがクーデターによる
スペイン本国からの独立をたくらんで
いたそうだ。君たちのおかげで
未然に防ぐことができたよ
speeches.English:
Apparently, Escante was planning 
 a coup to break away from Spain. 
 Thanks to you, we stopped it before
 it could happen.

speeches.Japanese: しかし、ひとつ気になることがある
speeches.English: But one concern remains.

speeches.Japanese:
エスカンテが探していた宝物の鍵が
最近、何者かによって新大陸の西岸に
持ち去られたという話を聞いたのだ
speeches.English:
I've heard that someone recently 
 took the key to the treasure 
 Escante was after to the west coast
 of the New World.

speeches.Japanese:
もしかして…
『証』の地図！
speeches.English: Could it be... the map to the Proof?

speeches.Japanese:
新大陸の西側か…
これは大変じゃ
speeches.English:
The western New World... 
 This won't be easy.

SC3 B278.summary: People posing as missionaries are exposed by a party led by an apparent magistrate. The governor and crew react differently to the staged intervention.

speeches.Japanese:
我ら総勢１００余名
イエズス会より派遣され
ただいま到着いたしました
speeches.English:
More than a hundred of us have just
 arrived. We were sent
 by the Society of Jesus.

speeches.Japanese:
おお、ご苦労であった
後日の謁見にそなえ
ゆっくりと休むがよいぞ
speeches.English:
Thank you for coming. Rest well
 before your audience 
 in the coming days.

speeches.Japanese: 待て待てーい！！
speeches.English: Halt!
Eh?

speeches.Japanese:
我らをたばかり、おそれ多くも
天子までもあざむかんとする
薄汚い密売人ども！！
speeches.English:
Filthy smugglers! You dare 
 deceive us, and even the Son 
 of Heaven himself!

speeches.Japanese: な、何だと！？
speeches.English: W-what!?

speeches.Japanese:
だまされてはならぬぞ！
そやつらは、近隣にて悪事を
働く小悪党の集団！
speeches.English:
Do not be fooled! They are petty 
 thugs who prey upon this region!

speeches.Japanese: くそっ、どういうことだ！
speeches.English: Damn it! What's going on?

speeches.Japanese: ま、まことか！？
speeches.English: Truly!?

speeches.Japanese:
濡れ衣でごさいます！
我々は正真正銘の…
speeches.English:
These accusations are false! 
 We are genuine...

speeches.Japanese:
ええい、だまれだまれ！！
そなたらの顔を覚えておる者が
密告してきたのじゃ！
speeches.English:
Silence! A witness who remembers 
 your faces reported you!

speeches.Japanese:
まんまと宣教師の一団に化けおおせ
このマカオにやって来たまでは
よかったが、猿芝居もそこまでじゃ！
speeches.English:
You reached Macao disguised
 as missionaries, 
 but this farce is over!

speeches.Japanese:
さあ、もう言い逃れはできぬぞ！
全員、引っ捕らえよ！！
speeches.English: No more excuses! Arrest them all!

speeches.Japanese: おおう！！
speeches.English: Yes, sir!

speeches.Japanese: ヒャッホゥ！！
speeches.English: Yahoo!

speeches.Japanese: せやッ！
speeches.English: Hah!

speeches.Japanese: ひ、ひいっ！
speeches.English: Eek!

speeches.Japanese:
チッ！
こんなところで、捕まるかよ！
speeches.English: Tch! I'm not getting caught here!

speeches.Japanese:
うーむ…。すっかりだまされて
危うくわしの首が飛ぶところであった
そなたらのおかげ……ん？
speeches.English:
Hmm... I was completely
 taken in. I nearly lost my head! 
 It is all thanks to you... Hm?

speeches.Japanese:
密売人の正体をあばいた軍勢は
どこへ消えたのじゃ？
speeches.English:
Where did the troops who 
 exposed them go?

speeches.Japanese:
え？
もう引き上げていきましたよ
speeches.English: They already withdrew, sir.

speeches.Japanese:
あ、左様か。ほう…
わしに挨拶もなしに？
…？？
speeches.English:
Oh...
 They left without a word to me?

speeches.Japanese:
しかし…
最近の明軍に
西洋人や日本人がおるとは…？
speeches.English:
But... Since when have there 
 been Westerners and Japanese 
 in the Ming army?

speeches.Japanese:
あの…、あんなもんで
よかったでしょうか？
speeches.English: Was that performance good enough?

speeches.Japanese:
驚いたわ
堂に入ったものね
speeches.English: Very convincing.

speeches.Japanese:
いやあ、傑作、傑作！
あのときの連中の顔ときたらねえぜ！
speeches.English:
Ha! That was priceless!
 You should've seen their faces!

speeches.Japanese:
そうそう！
マカオ総督なんて
完全に信じちゃってたもんね！
speeches.English:
Yes! Even Macao's governor believed
 every word!

speeches.Japanese:
さすがは、もと役者
街一番の物真似の名人じゃ
speeches.English:
Just what I would expect 
 from a former actor. The finest
 mimic in town!

speeches.Japanese: 県令の真似だなんて、おそれ多くて…
speeches.English:
Impersonating a magistrate...
 I hardly dared.

speeches.Japanese:
仕方がなかったのよ
向こうが変装で来るなら
こちらも対抗するしかないわ
speeches.English:
We had no choice. They used
 disguises, so we answered in kind.

speeches.Japanese:
これで、密売人組織も
しばらくはおとなしくなるじゃろう
…さて、おぬしはどうする？
speeches.English:
The smugglers should lie low 
 for a while. What will you do now?

speeches.Japanese:
どうもこうもありませんや
こうなったら、他に行くあてもねえ
俺はここで働かせてもらいやすぜ
speeches.English:
What else can I do? I've got 
 nowhere else to go now. I'll stay
 and work for you.

speeches.Japanese: いいわ。よろしくね
speeches.English: Welcome aboard.

SC3 B297.summary: Maria brings the man home to Guam. He thanks her and gives her a parting gift.

speeches.Japanese:
ここがグアムね…
待たせたわね、これで家に戻れるわよ
speeches.English:
This is Guam... Sorry to keep
 you waiting. You can go home now.

speeches.Japanese: シェシェ
speeches.English: Xiexie.

speeches.Japanese: えっ？　なあに？
speeches.English: What?

speeches.Japanese:
これを私に？
ああ、お礼にくれるのね
…ありがとう、いただくわ
speeches.English:
For me? Oh, it's a thank-you gift. 
 ...Thank you. I'd be happy 
 to accept it.

speeches.Japanese: シェシェ、シェシェ
speeches.English: Xiexie, xiexie!

speeches.Japanese:
元気でね
次に海に出るときは気をつけるのよ
speeches.English: Take care. Be careful when you sail.

gameplay.scope: Initialized Rafael script replay for both actor IDs. Ordinary controller inputs. Natural acquisition not exercised.
